findings.title: float: right on .small-action button is a no-op now that the parent is a flex container
findings.body: `.small-action` was changed to `@include flexbox()`, but the `button { float: right; }` rule inside it was kept. Floats are ignored on flex items, so the button (e.g. the 'change owner' / moderation button rendered in small actions) will no longer be pushed to the right edge; it will sit inline after the description as an ordinary flex item. The rule should be replaced with a flex-based right alignment (e.g. `margin-left: auto` on the button), otherwise the small-action button placement regresses visually on topic pages.

findings.title: Header right panel loses its right alignment on browsers using the legacy flexbox syntax
findings.body: The old `float: right` on `.d-header .panel` was replaced with `margin-left: auto`. `margin-left: auto` for end-alignment only works in the modern flexbox model; the 2009 box model that the `flexbox()` mixin also emits (`display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box`) does not honor auto margins — there you need `-webkit-box-pack: end` on the container. On any browser that only supports the old syntax (older Android/Safari that the prefixes were presumably added for), the login/sign-up panel will sit immediately after the title instead of being right-aligned, and since the floats were removed there is no fallback. Either add the box-pack fallback or keep a float-based fallback.

findings.title: Removal of .title float leaves no layout for browsers without flexbox support
findings.body: The diff deletes the `.d-header .contents .title { float: left; }` rule and replaces the layout entirely with the flexbox mixins on `.contents`. Browsers that support none of the five `display` variants emitted by `flexbox()` will fall back to block layout, where the title, extra-info and panel will each stack on their own line instead of laying out horizontally. If those browsers matter, a float fallback should be retained; otherwise the extra prefixed values serve no purpose.

findings.title: order() mixin mixes 2009 and 2012 spec syntaxes that don't work together
findings.body: The `order($val)` mixin emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` (2009 spec, integer-only, works only alongside `display: -webkit-box`) together with `-ms-flex-order`/`order`. In the corresponding layout files, `flexbox()` is applied to one element and `order(2)`/`order(3)` to different elements (.extra-info-wrapper, .panel), so within any single legacy engine only one of the pair of declarations applies and the reordering silently does nothing; also the 2009 engines require the group values to start at 1 (order 0 default vs. 2/3 here is fine, but the emitted 2009 declarations have no matching old-spec box on the sibling items). Practically this means visual order of the header contents differs between legacy and modern browsers; if legacy engines are not targeted, the 2009-era prefixes should be dropped from these mixins to avoid a false sense of compatibility.
